steps.description: BFS uses FIFO: enqueue start vertex 0.
BFS dequeues 0, so shallower discoveries leave first.
Discover 1 from 0 and enqueue it at the back.
Discover 2 from 0 and enqueue it at the back.
BFS dequeues 1, so shallower discoveries leave first.
Discover 3 from 1 and enqueue it at the back.
Discover 4 from 1 and enqueue it at the back.
BFS dequeues 2, so shallower discoveries leave first.
Discover 5 from 2 and enqueue it at the back.
BFS dequeues 3, so shallower discoveries leave first.
BFS dequeues 4, so shallower discoveries leave first.
Discover 6 from 4 and enqueue it at the back.
BFS dequeues 5, so shallower discoveries leave first.
BFS dequeues 6, so shallower discoveries leave first.
Reset. DFS uses LIFO: push start vertex 0.
DFS pops 0 and immediately follows its deepest pending branch.
Push 2 from 0. It is now above older branches.
Push 1 from 0. It is now above older branches.
DFS pops 1 and immediately follows its deepest pending branch.
Push 4 from 1. It is now above older branches.
Push 3 from 1. It is now above older branches.
DFS pops 3 and immediately follows its deepest pending branch.
DFS pops 4 and immediately follows its deepest pending branch.
Push 6 from 4. It is now above older branches.
DFS pops 6 and immediately follows its deepest pending branch.
DFS pops 2 and immediately follows its deepest pending branch.
Push 5 from 2. It is now above older branches.
DFS pops 5 and immediately follows its deepest pending branch.
Same start, different frontier rule. BFS: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]. DFS: [0, 1, 3, 4, 6, 2, 5].
